expected.description:
Available for Steam Deck

About the Game

WendyQuest is 100% fresh and 100% human made!

When mechanized monsters invade a culinary kingdom, it’s up to Wendy to save Savoria from mech-trouble. Welcome to WendyQuest, an epic original adventure where you earn real food as you play.

Play as Wendy and battle Mech Corp’s mechs, solve puzzles, and embark on an epic quest to unite four magical stones to save Savoria. Will you restore order to a realm in peril? The fate of flavor is in your hands.

Dr. Mechborg and his mechs have spread a curse called “Mechtosis” across Savoria using soggy fries, frozen beef & other culinary atrocities. Only Wendy - armed with sacred spatulas, fresh beef, and an ancient prophecy - can restore order to Savoria’s people and end the mechademic once and for all.

Square off against flavorless foes like Golden Archers, Hot Sludge Sundaes and other fast food fiends in strategic turn-based battles. Time your attacks perfectly to deal supersized damage.

Team up with tasty pals including a French Fry Archer, Spicy Chickeneer, Frosty Mage, and more. Each ally brings their own flavor to the table that deals extra damage against specific enemy types.

Journey across five food-themed regions including salty forests, seasoned deserts, rugged beefy bluffs, and Frosty-capped peaks - each filled with hidden secrets waiting to be discovered.

set.tagline: A fast-food fantasy that puts timed strikes and a scrappy party between you and a kingdom of deeply suspicious dinner.
set.description: WendyQuest is a free, single-player, turn-based adventure from 81monkeys. Guide Wendy and her food-themed allies through five regions, solve puzzles, and time attacks against Dr. Mechborg’s army. It runs on Windows through Steam and supports Xbox controllers.

systemRequirements.min: Windows 10. The developer lists 2 GB RAM and 500 MB free disk space. CPU and GPU models are not published; the Steam page uses joke placeholders instead of hardware specifications.
systemRequirements.recommended: Windows 10. The developer lists 4 GB RAM and 500 MB free disk space. Recommended CPU and GPU models are not published.

qualityBar.verdict: The joke gets you in; a well-timed spatula hit and a party worth arranging keep you playing.

set.longDescription:
WendyQuest could have stopped at the joke. A fast-food mascot picks up sacred spatulas, saves a kingdom from frozen beef, and calls its mechanical plague “Mechtosis.” That is enough premise for a promotional minigame. Instead, 81monkeys built a proper turn-based adventure around it, with a party to assemble, timed attacks to learn, puzzles to solve, and five regions to explore. The setting remains ridiculous. The useful surprise is that the combat asks you to pay attention.

Wendy sets out across Savoria after Dr. Mechborg’s machines put the realm in trouble. Each region gives the food puns a different landscape, from salty forests to cold peaks. The people you recruit are as committed to the bit as the world is: a French Fry Archer, a Spicy Chickeneer, and a Frosty Mage each bring a different edge to a fight. Choosing an ally is more than filling a portrait slot. Their strengths matter against particular enemies, so a good turn begins with a little thought about who should act next.

Then you have to land the attack. Timed inputs add a physical beat to encounters that might otherwise become a menu routine. The Steam description names Golden Archers and Hot Sludge Sundaes among the opposition, and it is hard to remain dignified while planning around either one. That contrast is the game's charm: a sincere RPG structure carrying a very unserious argument about dinner. Between battles, hidden corners and puzzles give you a reason to inspect each place instead of sprinting straight toward the next joke.

This is a focused, single-player Windows release. It is free through Steam, and the store lists full Xbox controller support. There is no online mode, dedicated server, or PlayBound party session to configure. The published hardware requirements are also playful to a fault: “Potato” and “Deep Fryer” are the listed processor and graphics entries, so we cannot turn them into a real CPU or GPU recommendation. Steam does give a Windows 10 floor, 2 GB minimum RAM, 4 GB recommended RAM, and 500 MB free space. Treat those numbers as store requirements, not a measured download size.

We like WendyQuest because it commits to its absurd premise without asking you to excuse thin play. The food jokes are the invitation; putting together a party and learning when to press are the parts that can make a free evening with it feel like time well spent. It is still a brand game, and you will know that from the first minute. It is also more interested in being an RPG than that label might lead you to expect.
set.whyWePickedIt: We picked WendyQuest because its brand joke leads into an actual little RPG: timed attacks, a party with distinct strengths, and regions worth exploring. Free promotional games rarely need you to think about your next turn. This one does, while remaining honest about its narrow Windows and single-player scope.
